title: Import a superseded or cancelled task's lifecycle change in task-folder sync instead of refusing it as unsupported_fields
outcome: Import a superseded or cancelled task's lifecycle change in task-folder sync instead of refusing it as unsupported_fields
acceptance: An incremental task-folder import applies a peer's supersede (lifecycle, superseded_by, disposal_reason) or cancellation of an existing task the importing store holds open and unclaimed, instead of refusing it as unsupported_fields; a task with live local execution is refused by name with the reason
An exact replay of the same folder changes nothing, and the export/import round trip between two stores leaves both with the same lifecycle, replacement link and reason
A behaviour test reproduces the 2026-11-27 case: store A supersedes an open task, exports; store B imports and shows it superseded by the same replacement

completion.summary: An incremental task-folder import now applies a peer's cancellation or supersession of a task the destination holds Open, as the ordinary Disposed event (lifecycle, replacement, reason), instead of refusing it as unsupported_fields. It is held as active_run under live local or descendant execution, refused as open_descendants while a descendant at any depth stays open (judged after the mixed-graph checks), and refused as durable_graph when a replacement closes a cycle through retired work. It ends a dormant run, lapsed claim and lapsed handoff offer and waives the departed holder, as local disposal does. Covered by storage tests (folder_apply::disposals, including the two-store round trip and exact repeat) and the two-host incremental CLI test. Landed as 4a7d8428 (FULL test-ea8f9fba PASS 12/12; independent evaluation 90389634 3/3). The round-5 ordering Medium is deferred to w-a45a8cba7e4c.
